quote.text: Remind thyself that he whom thou lovest is mortal  that what thou lovest is not thine own; it is given thee for the present, not irrevocably nor for ever, but even as a fig or a bunch of grapes at the appointed season of the year
quote.author: Epictetus
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood
    • Recognize the transient nature of each moment shared with your children; their youthful phases are gifts meant to be appreciated rather than taken for granted.
    • Understand that the love you nurture is both precious and impermanent, encouraging you to focus on the present and to cultivate memories that can sustain you through times of change.
  • Leadership
    • Accept that the connections and loyalties you build with your team are ephemeral—this awareness helps you lead with empathy and humility, knowing that each individual's contribution is a momentary blessing.
    • Embrace change and impermanence in relationships within your organization; this understanding fosters a leadership style grounded in gratitude, realism, and the adaptive virtue of letting go when needed.
  • Product Management
    • Realize that a product or feature, like a cherished loved one, is not an everlasting possession; it is an offering for the current market moment, prompting you to launch, learn, and iterate efficiently.
    • Keep in mind that every product release is time-bound and subject to evolution, encouraging you to treat feedback and market dynamics as opportunities to honor the fleeting nature of success and inspire continuous innovation.
